# Casual Game Recipe Book: 100 Documented Recipes from Simple to Stings — Intake Brief

**Work Item:** TF-0MUY9H7QZ000UX5W | **Type:** Epic | **Priority:** High

> **Headline:** Ship 100 new file-backed ToneGraph recipes with a casual, joyful
> game feel — ascending from single-oscillator blips to multi-layered musical
> stings — each with a matching `docs/recipe-book/` page written from both the
> sound-design and the ToneForge CLI perspective, so the whole recipe family
> doubles as a hands-on tour of the toolchain.

## Problem statement

ToneForge's recipe library is a growing but uneven set of sound families
(primarily card-game and MVP-era effects) with no single, curated body of
examples that teaches the tool by progressively introducing its capabilities.
Developers and sound designers lack an "ascending difficulty" reference that
takes them from the simplest possible synthesised sound to a layered musical
sting while showing, at each step, the exact CLI commands that produce,
inspect, vary, lay, and export it.

## Users

- **Game developers** prototyping casual/arcade games who need a large,
  coherent, joyful-sounding placeholder palette they can drop into a project.
- **Sound designers** and technical artists learning ToneForge who want a
  guided path from first principles to multi-layered composition.
- **ToneForge maintainers and documentation authors** who need a canonical,
  test-backed example set that demonstrates the full toolchain and keeps the
  docs honest.

Example user stories:

- As a game developer building a casual game, I want 100 ready-made procedural
  sounds spanning blips to stings, so that I can build a joyful audio identity
  without sourcing assets.
- As a sound designer new to ToneForge, I want each recipe documented from both
  the sound-design and CLI angles, so that I can understand *what* the sound is
  and *how* to reproduce and vary it with the tool.
- As a maintainer, I want automated tests linking every recipe to its
  documentation page, so the recipe book cannot silently drift from the code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **100 new file-backed ToneGraph recipes** exist under `presets/recipes/*.yaml`, each validating against the ToneGraph schema and discoverable via `toneforge list recipes`, with no changes to TypeScript recipe source required.
- **Monotonic complexity progression** across the defined tiers (see Scope): the set starts at single-oscillator primitives and ends at self-contained 2–3 voice melodic stings, with each tier illustrating the tooling stage appropriate to it (Q6/A).
- **Every recipe has a matching page** under `docs/recipe-book/` containing both a **Sound design** section (building blocks, parameters/ranges, seed behaviour, musical intent) and a **ToneForge CLI** section (copy-paste commands relevant to that recipe), and `docs/recipe-book/index.md` lists all 100 in ascending complexity order.
- **Capstone layered musical stings** are delivered as ToneGraph `presets/stacks/*.json` and `presets/sequences/*.json` that reuse the simpler recipes, documented with the corresponding `toneforge stack` / `toneforge sequence` commands (Q3/C, Q5/A).
- **Automated tests** validate: ToneGraph schema validity; deterministic rendering (same seed ⇒ byte-identical output); non-silence; recipe ↔ page bidirectional coverage (every recipe documented, every page backed by a recipe); and index completeness.
- **Aesthetic tagging** — every recipe carries `casual` / `fun` / `joy` tags (plus family-specific tags) and is filterable via `toneforge list recipes --tags casual` (Q4/C).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Scope

**In scope**

- 100 new ToneGraph YAML recipes, organised into ascending tiers:

  | Tier | Theme | Target count | Tooling illustrated |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | Pure tones & blips (single oscillator, simple envelope) | 14 | `generate`, `show`, `list recipes` |
  | 2 | Shaped events (envelope + pitch movement) | 14 | `generate`, `analyze` |
  | 3 | Textured & filtered (noise, filters, FM) | 16 | `classify`, `explore` |
  | 4 | Melodic motifs (2–4 note figures) | 14 | `sequence` (light), `library` |
  | 5 | Character & critter voices | 14 | `classify`, `visualize` |
  | 6 | Ambience & loops | 14 | `sequence`, `explore` |
  | 7 | Multi-voice stings (self-contained 2–3 voices) | 14 | `stack` concepts, `visualize` |
  | — | **Recipes subtotal** | **100** | — |
  | 8 | Capstone arrangements (additional artifacts) | ~8–10 stacks/sequences | `stack`, `sequence`, `mixer`, `tui` |

- A `docs/recipe-book/` index plus one page per recipe, following the existing
  docs front-matter convention (`title`, `id`, `order`, `description`).
- Tests backing AC 5, plus links from `README.md` / `demos/README.md` to the
  recipe book.
- Family-specific prefixes stay descriptive (e.g. `ui-`, `character-`,
  `impact-`, `collect-`), with the casual aesthetic expressed via tags (Q4/C).

**Out of scope**

- Final production audio assets (ToneForge generates placeholders by design).
- Changing the TypeScript recipe/registry architecture or the classifier
  vocabulary (a new `casual` category is explicitly *not* being added — Q4/C).
- A docs-site redesign; the recipe book reuses the current Markdown conventions.
- Promotion to `main` / release (owned by the `ship` skill).

## Constraints

- **Determinism:** same recipe + same seed ⇒ byte-identical output, across
  machines and runs.
- **Schema:** every recipe must pass ToneGraph validation (the same validation
  `toneforge library add` applies) and be discoverable without code changes.
- **No new `config.yaml` dependency:** because Q4/C avoids a new category,
  `.toneforge/config.yaml` need not be introduced.
- **Practical durations:** SFX remain short; stings stay within a few seconds so
  the full suite renders quickly.
- **UK English** throughout all documentation.
- **Documentation ↔ recipe integrity** must be mechanically enforced (AC 5), not
  maintained by hand.

## Existing state

- `presets/recipes/` holds 6 file-backed ToneGraph recipes
  (`ui-scifi-confirm`, `card-transform`, `footstep-gravel`, `weapon-laser-zap`,
  `ambient-wind-gust`, `frequency-sweep-demo`); the wider library is
  TypeScript-backed in `src/recipes/`.
- `presets/stacks/` (10) and `presets/sequences/` (28) already exist for the
  card-game family, providing worked examples of layer and timeline schemas.
- `docs/guides/external-recipes.md` documents file-backed recipe registration;
  `docs/tonegraph.md` documents the graph schema; `demos/README.md` documents
  walkthrough conventions.
- `.toneforge/` currently contains only `mixer/` (no `config.yaml`); built-in
  prefix→category defaults apply.
- There is no `docs/recipe-book/` directory and no recipe↔documentation
  coverage test.
- Closest precedent: the completed `Card Game Sound Effects Recipe Library`
  (TF-0MM65RIDV0EJH50O) — a tiered recipe epic that did the same for card games.

## Desired change

- Author 100 ToneGraph YAML recipes in `presets/recipes/`, tagged for the casual
  aesthetic and grouped into the tiers above.
- Author `docs/recipe-book/index.md` and one page per recipe, each with a
  Sound-design section and a ToneForge CLI section, ordered by ascending
  complexity.
- Author capstone stacks/sequences in `presets/stacks/` and
  `presets/sequences/` that compose the simpler recipes into layered musical
  stings.
- Add the coverage/determinism test battery (AC 5) and wire the recipe book into
  `README.md` and `demos/README.md`.
- Keep the CLI sections generated or template-checked where practical, so the
  commands cannot drift from the recipes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `presets/recipes/*.yaml` — 100 new file-backed ToneGraph recipes.
- `presets/stacks/*.json` — capstone layered-sting stacks (additional).
- `presets/sequences/*.json` — capstone arrangement sequences (additional).
- `docs/recipe-book/index.md` — ordered book index (new).
- `docs/recipe-book/<recipe-name>.md` — one page per recipe (new).
- `src/recipes/__tests__/` (or equivalent) — recipe↔page coverage and
  determinism tests for the book.
- `docs/tonegraph.md` — schema reference the recipes and book must match.
- `docs/guides/external-recipes.md` — file-backed registration reference.
- `README.md` / `demos/README.md` — discoverability links to the book.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: documentation drift.** 100 hand-written CLI sections can fall out of
  sync with the recipes. *Mitigation:* AC 5 enforces recipe↔page coverage in
  tests, and CLI command blocks are derived from recipe metadata/templates where
  practical.
- **Risk: scope creep.** "Everything in-between" invites an unbounded sound
  list. *Mitigation:* the tier table fixes 100 recipes and ~8–10 capstone
  arrangements; new ideas become separate `discovered-from` work items.
- **Risk: thin recipe variety.** 100 recipes could collapse into near-duplicates.
  *Mitigation:* tiers mandate distinct synthesis techniques (oscillator, pitch
  sweep, noise/filter, FM, multi-voice); reviews should reject copy-paste
  variants.
- **Risk: book authoring is large and repetitive** (100 pages).
  *Mitigation:* shared page template + index generation, with sound-design
  narrative authored per recipe and CLI blocks templated.
- **Risk: test-suite runtime** grows with 100 render checks.
  *Mitigation:* keep durations short and reuse a single render harness.
- **Assumption:** file-backed ToneGraph can express every required sound
  (including 2–3 voice stings) without new TypeScript recipes — consistent with
  the completed node/oscillator/filter/noise/FM surface (Q1/A).
- **Assumption:** the "casual game feel" is an aesthetic expressed through tags
  and sound-design intent, not a new category (Q4/C).
- **Assumption:** the existing docs front-matter convention
  (`title`/`id`/`order`/`description`) is the correct format for book pages.

## Related work (manual)

- `Card Game Sound Effects Recipe Library (TF-0MM65RIDV0EJH50O)` — completed
  epic; the closest structural precedent for a large, tiered recipe family.
- `Demo 1: Recipe Variety (TF-0MLXF74KE17SQKAD)` / `Recipe Variety Demo
  Walkthrough (TF-0MLYAO50U0DIOZI4)` — simplest-first showcase pattern.
- `Document the creation of a sound (TF-0MLYPJ9KO0NMWOMW)` — documentation
  conventions for sound creation.
- `demos/sound-creation.md` — the existing "sine wave → full recipe" tutorial
  this book extends in breadth.
- `demos/card-game-sounds.md` — walkthrough style for a large recipe family.
- `docs/guides/external-recipes.md`, `docs/tonegraph.md` — file-backed recipe
  authoring references.
- `Card Game Sequence/Stack Presets (TF-0MM79GCTT1CPF9F3)` — precedent for
  stack/sequence presets built over recipes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (recipe artefact format).** Which format should the 100 recipes use?
  - Options: (A) file-backed ToneGraph YAML in `presets/recipes/*.yaml`;
    (B) TypeScript recipes in `src/recipes/*.ts`; (C) mixed.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A.**
  - Rationale: the request is about illustrating the tooling; YAML recipes are
    discoverable and registerable purely through the CLI without code changes.

- **Q2 (documentation deliverable).** What shape should the documentation take?
  - Options: (A) one Markdown "recipe book" page per recipe plus an index;
    (B) executable walkthroughs in `demos/`; (C) a single combined cookbook.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A.**
  - Rationale: "each sound fully documented" maps naturally to a per-recipe page
    with sound-design and CLI narratives side by side.

- **Q3 (layering approach).** How should the layered stings be realised?
  - Options: (A) ToneGraph stacks/sequences reusing simpler recipes;
    (B) self-contained multi-voice recipes; (C) mix.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): C.**
  - Rationale: small stings stay portable as single recipes; the largest
    arrangements demonstrate the composition tooling.

- **Q4 (category & naming).** How should the casual aesthetic be represented?
  - Options: (A) existing prefixes/categories plus `casual` tags; (B) a new
    `casual` category via `.toneforge/config.yaml`; (C) hybrid — descriptive
    family prefixes plus a `casual` tag.

    descriptive prefixes keep category classification accurate. `.toneforge/`
    currently has no `config.yaml`.

- **Q5 (what the 100 counts).** Does "100" include stacks/sequences?
  - Options: (A) 100 sound recipes, with stacks/sequences additional;
    (B) 100 total artifacts; (C) flexible.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A.**

  - Options: (A) progressive — each tier/recipe shows the pipeline stage
    appropriate to it; (B) core only; (C) every surface for every recipe.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A.**

# Recipe Book Harness & Tracer Slice

> **Goal:** Provide the manifest-driven tooling and test battery that makes the 100-recipe book
> mechanically verifiable, and prove the whole pipeline end-to-end with one real recipe + page
> (a tracer bullet through every layer: recipe data, generator, docs, index, tests).

## Context

The book must not be able to drift from the code (AC 5). This feature builds the *machinery*
before any bulk authoring: a single roster manifest that declares all 100 planned recipes
(so later tiers only add entries), a page template, generators for the index and the
ToneForge CLI command blocks, and a test battery run against every *delivered* roster entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/recipes/recipe-book/roster.ts` type-checks and declares all 100 planned recipes with `name`, `tier`, `family` and a one-line sound-design intent; tier counts are 14/14/16/14/14/14/14 = 100.
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-index.ts` and `scripts/recipe-book/generate-cli-blocks.ts` run via `tsx`, are idempotent (second run produces byte-identical output), and fail loudly on a delivery gap.
- `docs/recipe-book/_template.md` defines the page shape: front matter (`title`, `id`, `order`, `description`), a hand-authored `## Sound design` section, and a `## ToneForge CLI` section whose command block sits between machine-readable markers.
- `src/recipes/__tests__/recipe-book.test.ts` asserts, for every delivered roster entry: ToneGraph schema validity; byte-identical determinism at a fixed seed; non-silence; a matching `docs/recipe-book/<name>.md` page; presence in `docs/recipe-book/index.md` in roster order; required tags (`casual` plus at least one of `fun`/`joy`, plus a family tag); and CLI-block freshness (regeneration matches the committed block).
- The tracer recipe `presets/recipes/blip-sine-ping.yaml` and page `docs/recipe-book/blip-sine-ping.md` are delivered and pass every gate above.
- `docs/recipe-book/index.md` is generated from delivered entries in roster order; the full project suite passes (`npm test`).


Parent acceptance-criteria traceability:
- Traces to parent AC 2: **Monotonic complexity progression** across the defined tiers (see Scope): the set starts at single-oscillator primitives and ends at self-contained 2–3 voice melodic stings, with each tier illustrating the tooling stage appropriate to it (Q6/A).
- Traces to parent AC 3: **Every recipe has a matching page** under `docs/recipe-book/` containing both a **Sound design** section (building blocks, parameters/ranges, seed behaviour, musical intent) and a **ToneForge CLI** section (copy-paste commands relevant to that recipe), and `docs/recipe-book/index.md` lists all 100 in ascending complexity order.
- Traces to parent AC 5: **Automated tests** validate: ToneGraph schema validity; deterministic rendering (same seed ⇒ byte-identical output); non-silence; recipe ↔ page bidirectional coverage (every recipe documented, every page backed by a recipe); and index completeness.
## Minimal Implementation

- Author the roster manifest with all 100 names/tiers/families/intents (roster is fixed in the parent plan).
- Author the page template and the two generator scripts (reuse `gray-matter` for front matter).
- Author the test battery; scope coverage assertions to roster entries that are delivered so
  every later tier stays green, with the "all 100 delivered" gate deferred to the completion feature.
- Author the tracer recipe + page and regenerate the index.

## Key Files

- `src/recipes/recipe-book/roster.ts` — canonical 100-entry roster manifest (new).
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-index.ts` — index generator (new).
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-cli-blocks.ts` — CLI-block generator/validator (new).
- `docs/recipe-book/_template.md` — page template (new).
- `docs/recipe-book/index.md` — generated ordered index (new).
- `src/recipes/__tests__/recipe-book.test.ts` — coverage/determinism/tag/CLI-freshness battery (new).
- `presets/recipes/blip-sine-ping.yaml` — tracer recipe (new).
- `docs/recipe-book/blip-sine-ping.md` — tracer page (new).

## Dependencies

None — this is the first feature and unblocks all tiers.

## Deliverables

Roster manifest; two generator scripts; page template; generated index; test battery;
one complete tracer recipe + page.

resolve → render → play pipeline, but it drives the runtime from a *scripted,
deterministic clock* and exits. The PRD's runtime is a **live, event-driven
engine a host embeds at run time** (RUNTIME_PRD §3 primary goals, §5 playback
modes, §6 API, §19 pipeline). This item delivers the first live slice: a real
clock, interactive input, a bounded buffer cache, and playback scheduled on the
host audio path.

## User Story

As a game developer, I want to drive the runtime with live state and context
changes and hear it react immediately (walk → sprint, stone → gravel), so that
the runtime behaves as an embeddable real-time engine rather than a scripted
offline replay.

## Scope

**In scope**

1. **Live host clock** — the session uses the real clock by default (no faked
   step clock); `setState`/`setContext` take effect immediately.
2. **Interactive command surface** — `toneforge runtime start` REPL
   (`state <name>`, `context <dim>=<value>`, `inspect`, `reset`, `help`, `quit`),
   plus `--script <file>` for deterministic non-interactive replay and `--json`
   for headless event streaming.
3. **Bounded LRU buffer cache** keyed by `(recipe, seed, overrides)`
   (RUNTIME_PRD §19.5); bounded and deterministically evicting.
4. **Real playback scheduling** — each resolved event's buffer is scheduled at
   its sequence-relative time on the host playback path (Node `playAudio`;
   browser `AudioBufferSourceNode`), cancellable on stop/quit.

**Out of scope** (follow-up item, blocked by this one)

5. Audible `setSfxParameter` modulation of a continuous/looping voice (§19.9).
6. Long-running / service mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `toneforge runtime start` accepts interactive commands (`state <name>`,
   `context <dim>=<value>`, `inspect`, `reset`, `help`, `quit`) and applies each
   to the live runtime immediately; invalid commands/state/context produce
   actionable errors and do **not** terminate the session.
2. The session uses a live clock by default; `--script <file>` replays a
   command sequence non-interactively and exits `0`.
3. `--json` streams one JSON object per runtime event to stdout (no pretty
   output, no audio), verifiable in CI without audio hardware.
4. A bounded LRU buffer cache caches renders keyed by `(recipe, seed, overrides)`;
   repeated `(recipe, seed)` events reuse a cached buffer, eviction is
   deterministic (LRU), and the cache never exceeds its configured bound.
5. Resolved events are scheduled for playback at their sequence-relative time via
   an injectable scheduler, rendered through the cache, and played on the host
   path; scheduled playback is cancelled on `quit`/`stop`.
6. Determinism: replaying the same `--script` with the same seed reproduces the
   same event log.
7. Documentation updated (`RUNTIME_PRD`, README, CLI help, browser usage); the
   full test suite passes.

## References

- `docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md` §3, §5, §6, §19
- `src/runtime/runtime.ts`, `src/runtime/audio.ts`, `src/runtime/scenario.ts`
- `docs/browser-usage.md`

# Runtime session: continuous footsteps transport with start/stop

child-of:TF-0MM4OWRQ70IWEKZ2
depends-on:TF-0MUYBRKAT0036X2A
discovered-from:TF-0MUYBRKAT0036X2A

## Summary

The live session (TF‑0MUYBRKAT0036X2A) applies `state`/`context` commands
immediately, but each command fires a **one-shot** pattern: `state walk` plays
three footsteps and stops. The PRD's runtime is meant to sustain behavioural
audio (§5 playback modes), so this item adds a **continuous transport**: a
`start`/`stop` control that keeps the active sequence looping, and re-resolves
sequence (state) and recipe (context) on every iteration so the sound changes
live while it plays.

This is the MVP demo for "footsteps that keep going and adapt to commands".
Full real-time parameter automation and daemonised service mode stay in the
follow-up TF‑0MUYBRRCQ00148QD (which depends on this work for the re-render
seam).

## User Story

As a game developer, I want to start continuous footsteps and then change state
and environment on the fly — hearing the cadence and surface switch while the
pattern keeps playing — so that the runtime demonstrates sustained behavioural
audio, not just isolated bursts.

## Scope

**In scope**

1. `start [state]` / `stop` session commands controlling a looping transport.
2. Continuous iteration of the active sequence via the injectable scheduler,
   re-arming after the pattern period.
3. Live reconfiguration: `state` swaps the looped sequence, `context`
   re-resolves recipes on subsequent iterations.
4. Per-iteration seed variation (deterministic, derived from the iteration
   index) with a toggle.
5. A bounded-run option (`maxIterations`; CLI `--iterations`) so scripted and
   `--json` runs terminate.
6. Cancellation on `stop`/`quit`/`reset`; no orphaned timers.

**Out of scope** (follow-up TF‑0MUYBRRCQ00148QD)

- Audible `setSfxParameter` modulation (intensity/gain/pitch/filter).
- Long-running/service (daemon) mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The session accepts `start [state]` and `stop`; `start` begins/continues a
   looping transport for the active sequence, `stop` halts it and cancels
   pending playback; malformed usage reports an error without terminating the
   session.
2. While the transport runs, a `state` change switches the looped sequence
   (walk→run→sprint) and a `context` change re-resolves recipes
   (footstep-stone→footstep-gravel) on subsequent iterations, with no session
   restart.
3. Iterations use a distinct, deterministic per-iteration event seed derived
   from the iteration index; the variation is toggleable, and when disabled all
   iterations are identical.
4. Determinism: with a virtual clock and an injected scheduler, a fixed command
   sequence plus seed reproduces the same event log and the same iteration seed
   sequence (verifiable in CI without audio hardware).
5. `maxIterations` (CLI `--iterations`) stops the transport automatically after
   the configured number of iterations, so scripted/`--json` runs terminate;
   interactive runs are unbounded until `stop`/`quit`.
6. Playback remains scheduled at sequence-relative times through the buffer
   cache; `stop`/`quit`/`reset` cancel the loop and all pending playback with no
   orphaned timers.
7. Documentation updated; the full project test suite passes.

## References

- `docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md` §5 (playback modes), §19.5 (buffer cache), §19.10 (live session)
- `src/runtime/session.ts`, `src/runtime/runtime.ts`, `src/runtime/buffer-cache.ts`
- TF‑0MUYBRKAT0036X2A (live session this builds on)
- TF‑0MUYBRRCQ00148QD (follow-up: parameter modulation + service mode)

# implement.py drive: child sessions escape the worktree and pollute the main checkout

discovered-from:TF-0MUY9H7QZ000UX5W

## Summary

`implement.py drive <epic>` spawns a fresh `pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve`
session per child with `cwd=<child worktree>`. Observed during the Casual Game
Recipe Book epic (TF-0MUY9H7QZ000UX5W): the spawned child session had the correct
cwd recorded in its session metadata but performed **all** file writes against the
**main checkout** (`/home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge`), not the worktree.

## Reproduction

1. `python3 implement.py drive TF-0MUY9H7QZ000UX5W` from the main checkout.
2. The drive starts child TF-0MUYBDMHM003TI3D, creating
   `.worklog/worktrees/wl-TF-0MUYBDMHM003TI3D-tier-1-pure-tones-blips`.
3. The child session's JSONL session metadata records
   `"cwd":"…/.worklog/worktrees/wl-TF-0MUYBDMHM003TI3D-tier-1-pure-tones-blips"`.
4. The child's first bash command is `cd /home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge && …`
   and every subsequent `write` uses absolute main-checkout paths, e.g.
   `write /home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge/presets/recipes/tone-sine-mid-click.yaml`.
5. The worktree stays clean; the main checkout accumulates new recipe files.

## Impact

- Violates the mandatory worktree isolation invariant.
- `implement.py finish` refuses when changes exist outside the worktree, so the
  child cannot complete — the drive loop then fails.
- The interrupted child `pi` process was orphaned (`ppid=1`) after the drive was
  stopped and **kept writing to the main checkout** until killed manually,
  repeatedly re-polluting a cleaned tree.

## Secondary observation

When `finish` failed at the `push` step it still removed the child worktree
(the branch and commit survived, so work was recoverable, but the working tree
was lost). Cleanup should not run on a failed push, or should be clearly
reported.

## Suggested investigation

- Confirm the child session inherits `cwd` at process start (it appears to).
- Anchor the child agent to the worktree explicitly in the drive prompt (e.g.
  prepend "Work ONLY inside <worktree>; never write to the main checkout.").
- Ensure the drive kills the whole child process group on timeout/interrupt so
  no orphaned session can keep writing.
- Guard `finish` cleanup behind a successful push.

# Runtime scenario: one footstep per sequence with explicit loopInterval

child-of:TF-0MM4OWRQ70IWEKZ2
depends-on:TF-0MUYF87JH0089VQO
discovered-from:TF-0MUYF87JH0089VQO

## Summary

The runtime demo sequences currently carry three `footstep` events each; the
events double as the cadence carrier (the transport derives its loop period
from the event timing). With the continuous transport now in place, each
sequence should represent a **single footstep** and declare its loop cadence
explicitly via a new optional `loopInterval` (seconds) field, so one iteration
= one footstep and the per-state cadence is a first-class value rather than an
emergent property of event timing.

## User Story

As a game developer, I want each runtime sequence to be one footstep with an
explicit loop interval, so that the transport plays one footstep per iteration
and the walk/run/sprint cadence is defined in one obvious place.

## Scope

**In scope**

1. Add optional `loopInterval` (seconds, > 0) to the sequence preset schema
   (`SequencePresetJson` / `SequenceDefinition`), validated and parsed.
2. Change `presets/runtime/footsteps.json` so each state sequence has exactly
   one `footstep` event and an explicit `loopInterval` (walk `0.6`, run `0.35`,
   sprint `0.25`).
3. Make the transport use the active sequence's `loopInterval` as its loop
   period when present, falling back to the event-derived period otherwise.
4. Update tests and docs.

**Out of scope**

- Any change to `setSfxParameter` / service mode (TF‑0MUYBRRCQ00148QD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `SequencePresetJson` / `SequenceDefinition` support an optional positive
   `loopInterval` in seconds; validation rejects non-numeric or non-positive
   values, and parsing preserves a valid value (including through the JSON
   preset loader).
2. `presets/runtime/footsteps.json` defines exactly one `footstep` event per
   state sequence, with `loopInterval` `0.6` (walk), `0.35` (run) and `0.25`
   (sprint).
3. The continuous transport loops at the active sequence's `loopInterval` when
   present (falling back to the event-derived period otherwise); a state change
   picks up the new interval on the next iteration.
4. Tests cover: `loopInterval` validation/parse, transport period selection
   from `loopInterval`, one footstep per state activation/iteration, and the
   updated CLI event counts.
5. Documentation updated (sequence schema/PRD, `RUNTIME_PRD.md` §19.10,
   `demos/runtime.md`); the full project test suite passes.

- `src/sequence/schema.ts`, `src/sequence/preset-loader.ts`

- `presets/runtime/footsteps.json`
- `docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md` §19.10, `docs/prd/SEQUENCER_PRD.md`

## Summary

Two defects in the recipe-book harness shipped by the tracer slice (TF-0MUYBDM4X005O4N8):

1. **Vacuous per-recipe gate.** `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` computed `var isDelivered = existsSync(yamlPath)` inside a `for (var k ...)` loop and passed it into a deferred Vitest `describe()` callback. Because `var` is function-scoped and Vitest defers describe callbacks, every callback observed the *last* iteration's value. With the last roster entry undelivered, the entire 'delivered entries only' gate (schema, registry, non-silence, determinism, page, index, tags, CLI markers) was skipped for all recipes.

2. **Index order violated the AC.** `scripts/recipe-book/generate-index.ts` re-sorted within tier by `localeCompare`, producing alphabetical order, while the parent AC and the index-order gate require the roster's ascending-complexity order.

## Fix

- Use block scoping (`let k`, `const entry/recipeName/yamlPath/isDelivered`) so each describe captures its own values (commit with Tier 5).
- Sort the index by tier only, preserving the roster's authored within-tier order (commit with Tier 5).

## Verification

`npx vitest run src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` now executes 609 real gate assertions (was 105 vacuous) and passes for all delivered tiers.

# Intake Brief: Show parameters when generating

**Work Item:** TF-0MUYMTMVT001U573 | **Priority:** Medium | **Type:** feature

> **Summary:** Display the seed-derived parameter values used during generation in both human-readable and JSON output for `tf generate --recipe <name>`.

## Problem Statement

When generating sounds with `tf generate`, the recipe's parameters are set by the RNG using the seed, but these values are never exposed to the user. Users cannot know what parameter values were used for a given seed, making it difficult to reproduce or iterate on generated sounds.

## Users

**Developers using ToneForge** to generate and inspect procedural sounds.

### User Stories

- As a developer, I want to see the parameter values that were used for a given seed, so I can reproduce the sound or adjust parameters intentionally.
- As a developer, I want parameter values in both human-readable and JSON output, so I can use them programmatically or read them in a terminal.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tf generate --recipe <name> --seed <n>` (human-readable mode) displays the seed-derived parameter values alongside the existing output (recipe name, seed, WAV write confirmation). Each parameter is shown as `name: value unit` (e.g. `filterFreq: 842 Hz`).
2. `tf generate --recipe <name> --seed <n> --json` (JSON mode) outputs valid JSON containing `recipe`, `seed`, `duration`, and a `params` object keyed by parameter name with numeric values.
3. For batch generation (`--seed-range`), parameter values are displayed per-seed: in human-readable mode one block per seed; in JSON mode an array of per-seed objects, each containing `seed`, `duration`, and `params`.
4. The existing `--output` flag for WAV file writing continues to work unchanged.
5. When no seed is provided (random seed), the random seed value and its parameters are still displayed.
6. Human-readable output uses the `ParamDescriptor` units for each parameter (e.g. Hz, s, amplitude, ratio).

## Constraints

- Must work with all registered recipes (built-in and file-backed).
- JSON output should be machine-parseable (no extra text).
- Human-readable output should be concise — list parameter names and values with units from the `ParamDescriptor`.
- Must not break existing CLI consumers that parse the output.

## Existing State

- `src/cli/commands/generate.ts` — the generate command handler renders audio and outputs metadata but does not expose parameters.
- `src/core/renderer.ts` — `renderRecipe` returns `RenderResult` (samples, sampleRate, duration, numberOfChannels) but does not expose parameter values.
- `src/recipes/index.ts` — each recipe registration includes a `params: ParamDescriptor[]` array and a `getParams(rng)` function that returns `{ [name]: number }`.
- `src/cli/commands/show.ts` — already uses `getParams` to display parameters for the `tf show` command.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/cli/commands/generate.ts` — add parameter display logic to the handler
- `src/core/renderer.ts` — extend `RenderResult` or create a new return type that includes parameter values
- `src/core/recipe.ts` — the `RecipeRegistration` interface (no changes needed; `getParams` already exists)
- `src/output.ts` — if new formatting helpers are needed for parameter display

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** The `--json` flag exists but is currently unimplemented; this change makes it functional. Scripts expecting invalid JSON will break — but this is acceptable as the flag was a no-op.
- **Risk:** Changing output format could break scripts that parse human-readable output. Mitigation: keep the existing metadata lines (recipe name, seed, file write) intact; only add parameter lines.
- **Assumption:** Parameter values are derived from the same RNG used by the renderer, ensuring consistency between output and the rendered audio.
- **Assumption:** For `--seed-range`, all seeds produce valid recipes; invalid seeds are not expected.

## Related Work

- **TF-0MLYNZWQU1X2LGZW** — Add a `tf show <recipe>` command (completed). This work item is complementary: `tf show` inspects a recipe, while `tf generate` should also expose parameters in its output.

# Intelligence conformance harness

## Goal

Provide one deterministic, reusable harness that every ToneForge Intelligence engine is validated against, so `audit`, `recommend` and `suggest-exploration` cannot drift in output shape, determinism, or read-only behaviour.

**Parent:** Demo 11: Intelligence -- Assisted Decision-Making (TF-0MLXF98WZ1LQGM5W). **Depends on:** nothing (first slice).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture library is committed under `src/test-utils/fixtures/intelligence/` containing at least one category with a coverage gap, one redundancy cluster (>=3 perceptually similar entries), and one quality issue (e.g. clipping or silence).
- The harness runs every Intelligence engine against the fixture library with a fixed seed and asserts byte-identical output across two consecutive runs (determinism).
- The harness asserts that running any Intelligence command leaves every file in the fixture library byte-identical (read-only guarantee).
- The harness asserts the JSON output contract (stable required keys, types, and `confidence` within [0,1] where present) for `intelligence audit`, `intelligence recommend`, and `intelligence suggest-exploration`.
- `npm test` passes and the harness fails loudly if any contract assertion regresses.

## Implementation sketch

- Fixtures: small deterministic entries under `src/test-utils/fixtures/intelligence/` plus a README describing each planted gap/redundancy/quality issue.
- `src/intelligence/__tests__/conformance.test.ts` driving shared assertion helpers.
- Shared helpers for byte-compare, library-snapshot hashing and JSON-shape assertions.

**Key Files:**

- `src/intelligence/__tests__/conformance.test.ts`
- `src/test-utils/fixtures/intelligence/README.md`
- `src/test-utils/buffer-compare.ts`

## Deliverables

Fixtures, harness, contract tests, brief README note.

# Library audit engine + `intelligence audit`

## Goal

As a developer managing a sound library, I want `toneforge intelligence audit --library <dir>` to report coverage gaps, redundancy and quality issues, so I can see what my collection is missing and where it is bloated.

**Parent:** Demo 11: Intelligence -- Assisted Decision-Making (TF-0MLXF98WZ1LQGM5W). **Depends on:** Intelligence conformance harness.

- `toneforge intelligence audit --library <dir>` identifies coverage gaps, redundancy, and quality issues in the target library and exits 0 (parent AC1).

- Every finding includes at least one actionable CLI command valid against the real CLI surface (e.g. `toneforge explore sweep --recipe <r> --seed-range <a:b> --rank-by <metric>`, `toneforge library search --category <c>`).
- `--json` emits a structured report and human output is readable; unit tests cover gap/redundancy/quality detection and the actionable-command contract, and integration tests cover the CLI.

# Safety, determinism & explainability hardening

## Goal

Prove — not assume — that Intelligence is assistive only: it never mutates library data, logs every recommendation, and exposes one consistent confidence/rationale contract.

**Parent:** Demo 11: Intelligence -- Assisted Decision-Making (TF-0MLXF98WZ1LQGM5W). **Depends on:** Library audit engine, Recommendation engine, Exploration suggestion engine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No Intelligence action modifies library data without human approval (parent AC4); directory-hash tests prove no `intelligence` command writes to the library.
- `--dry-run` is supported, and is the default behaviour, wherever a write could otherwise occur; no command mutates library data without explicit human approval.
- Every recommendation/audit finding is logged with rationale and affected assets.
- The confidence/rationale contract is identical across `audit`, `recommend`, and `suggest-exploration` (same field names, ranges, and explanation shape).
- Docs (`README` / `docs/`) state the read-only guarantee and the human-in-the-loop rule.
- `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Implementation sketch

- Read-only guards + snapshot hashing utilities.
- Recommendation logging + `--dry-run` flag plumbing.
- Shared contract types in `src/intelligence/types.ts` with contract tests.
- Doc updates.

# Verify: Memory core types & append-only store

## Goal

Provide test-first verification that the Memory record schema and its
append-only, project-local store meet the PRD contract before implementation
begins.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Memory record schema validation rejects malformed records and accepts the PRD record shape (timestamp, module, event, details, confidence, category, version, attribution).
- The store is append-only: a second write appends and never mutates or deletes prior records.
- Memory records are project-local under `.toneforge/memory/`; no global or cross-project reads/writes occur.
- Records are versioned, timestamped and attributable; identical inputs with a frozen clock produce byte-identical output (determinism).
- A clock seam is injectable so time-scoped assertions are not time-dependent.
- Memory generation, promotion and rejection events are recorded as append-only, timestamped, attributable records.

## Minimal Implementation

- Author `src/memory/__tests__/store.test.ts` and schema tests using a fixture record set.
- Use an injected clock and a temp store directory; assert byte-identical output across repeat runs.
- Assert no file changes occur outside the temp store (read-only guarantee for reads).

- Demo 11 Intelligence (`TF-0MLXF98WZ1LQGM5W`) — epic-level hard prerequisite.

- Failing-first tests for Memory schema, append-only semantics, project-local isolation and determinism.

# Verify: Intent submit, approval gate & memory-aware Intelligence

# Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry

## Goal

Provide the deterministic, offline test foundation for the Marketplace slice so every
later feature is verified by a shared harness over fixture packages rather than a live
network.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A deterministic conformance harness runs with **no live network access** and fails
   if any marketplace test attempts one.
2. A fixture registry plus package fixtures cover: a valid publishable package, an
   invalid-manifest package, a version-conflict package, and a package with a missing
   dependency.
3. The harness asserts search listings, install registration, publish rejection,
   version-conflict detection and post-install determinism (same seed => byte-identical
   output).
4. The harness is wired into `npm test` and the full project test suite (`npm test`)
   passes with the marketplace changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `src/test-utils/fixtures/marketplace/` with a fixture registry directory and the
  valid/invalid package fixtures.
- Add fixture loader helpers mirroring existing `src/test-utils/` conventions.
- Add `src/marketplace/conformance.test.ts` (written first, initially failing) that
  exercises the five behaviours above through the marketplace public API.
- No live network; the fixture registry is the only backend used.

## Deliverables

- Fixture registry and package fixtures.
- Reusable fixture loader helpers.
- Conformance harness test file wired into the suite.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first foundation).

## Goal

Test-first foundation for the Network module: a deterministic conformance harness and
fixture set that prove two independent clients resolve identical behavioural output from
the same behavioural-event stream, and that measure per-event network cost.

## What the user sees

Running the network conformance suite proves, offline, that the same event stream yields
byte-identical resolved sound parameters on two clients, and prints the measured bytes
per event / projected bandwidth.

## Minimal implementation

- Fixture set of behavioural event sequences under `src/test-utils/fixtures/network/walk-run.json`
  (walk -> run transition, context change, late-join stream).
- A resolver abstraction (two independent instances) that turns an event into a
  deterministic resolved-output descriptor.
- Harness that replays a fixture through both resolvers and compares output, plus a
  byte-accounting helper for serialized events.
- Negative control: a deliberately seed-mismatched stream asserts the harness fails.

## Key Files

- `src/network/__tests__/conformance.test.ts` — New: replay/compare harness tests.
- `src/test-utils/fixtures/network/walk-run.json` — New: behavioural event fixtures.
- `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md` — Sections 4, 9, 10 (events, determinism, performance).

## Constraints

- Offline and deterministic: no live sockets in unit/conformance tests.
- Reuse existing test-utils patterns (`src/test-utils/`).
- TypeScript strict; `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A fixture set of behavioural event sequences (walk -> run, context change, late join)
   exists under `src/test-utils/fixtures/network/walk-run.json`.
2. The harness feeds the same event stream to two independent client resolvers and
   asserts byte-identical resolved output, with a negative control proving it fails when
   seeds differ.
3. The harness measures serialized bytes per event and projects a typical gameplay stream
   below 1 KB/s (parent AC2).
4. Tests run offline and deterministically and are included in `npm test`.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Risky assumptions

- The resolved-output descriptor shape is a planning-time decision; if it changes, only
  the harness/fixtures change.
data.title: Network determinism and bandwidth conformance harness

## Goal

context snapshot) and its canonical serialization, shared by host and clients.

A documented event type that serializes to a compact canonical form and round-trips
exactly; unknown event versions are rejected gracefully.

## Minimal implementation

- `BehaviouralEvent` types + validation (`event`, `seed`, `time`, `state`, `context`).
- Canonical, deterministic encode/decode (stable key order) with a version field.
- Forward-compatible dispatch: unknown versions are skipped with a structured warning.
- Unit tests for round-trip, malformed input and unknown version.

## Key Files

- `src/network/types.ts` — New: behavioural event and snapshot types.
- `src/network/events.ts` — New: canonical serialization + version handling.

- Events are compact: keep the encoded form bounded and documented.

## Acceptance Criteria

   Section 4.1.
2. Canonical serialization is deterministic (stable ordering) and round-trips exactly.

## Goal

Implement transport-agnostic host/join and broadcast for behavioural events, with a
WebSocket adapter that reuses the existing `ws` dependency, under a host-authoritative
model for the demo.

## What the user sees

`network.host({ port })` starts a host session; `network.join("host:port")` connects a
client; the host broadcasts state changes and each peer receives them in a deterministic
order.

## Minimal implementation

- Transport interface with an in-memory adapter (tests) and a WebSocket adapter (runtime).
- `host()` / `join()` session lifecycle + peer registry (connect/disconnect).
- Host-authoritative broadcast of behavioural events; non-host peers relay only.
- Tests use the in-memory adapter; one integration test exercises the WebSocket adapter.

## Key Files

- `src/network/session.ts` — New: host/join lifecycle, peer registry, authority.
- `src/network/transport.ts` — New: transport interface + in-memory adapter.
- `src/network/ws-transport.ts` — New: WebSocket adapter (reuses `ws`).
- `src/network/index.ts` — New: public module surface.
- `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md` — Sections 4.3, 7 (authority, API).

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing `ws` dependency (already used by `web/server`); add no new runtime
  dependency.
- The core must not depend on the WebSocket implementation (injectable transport).
- No live network in unit tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `network.host()` starts a host session and `network.join()` connects a client, with
   connection lifecycle events emitted.
2. The host broadcasts behavioural events to all connected peers; a peer receives them in
   deterministic order.
3. Authority is host-authoritative and documented; non-host peers do not emit
   authoritative events.
4. The peer registry tracks connect/disconnect and removes dropped peers.
5. Tests use an in-memory adapter plus one WebSocket integration test; full project test
   suite passes.

## Risky assumptions

- Browser WebSocket client support is sufficient for the demo (no Node-only transport
  needed in the browser).

## Goal

Late-joining clients receive a state snapshot and converge to the live state, with
timestamp correction and bounded drift compensation under jitter.

## What the user sees

A client that joins after playback has started receives a snapshot, immediately plays the
correct current output, and stays aligned as further transitions arrive.

## Minimal implementation

- Snapshot request/response on join (current state + context + seed).
- Timestamp correction and ordering for out-of-order/late events.
- Bounded drift compensation with documented tolerance and graceful degradation.
- Tests for late join, reordered delivery and simulated jitter using the harness.

## Key Files

- `src/network/snapshot.ts` — New: snapshot capture/apply on join.
- `src/network/sync.ts` — New: timestamp correction, ordering, drift compensation.
- `src/network/__tests__/sync.test.ts` — New: late-join/reorder/jitter tests.
- `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md` — Section 8 (latency and drift handling).

## Constraints

- Bounded divergence: drift compensation must never cause unbounded state jumps.
- Deterministic given the same delivered event order.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On join, the host sends a state snapshot and the late joiner resolves the current state
   and plays the correct deterministic output (parent AC5).
2. Out-of-order/late events are ordered by timestamp; drift compensation is bounded and
   documented.
3. Under simulated jitter the two clients remain aligned within a documented tolerance
   (harness assertion).
4. Tests cover late join, reordering and jitter; full project test suite passes.

## Risky assumptions

- The demo tolerance for perceptual alignment can be expressed in the resolved-output
  descriptor; if not, a documented fallback threshold is used.
data.title: Late-join snapshot and drift/latency handling

data.description:
## Goal

Installed Marketplace recipes are registered only in the installing process's recipe registry and recorded as metadata in the library index; a subsequent `toneforge generate --recipe <installed>` / `toneforge stack render` process cannot resolve them. This violates the Demo 16 epic acceptance criterion 2 ("installed recipes render via `toneforge generate --recipe <installed>`") and makes the documented post-install workflow fail.

Discovered while implementing TF-0MUZX3ZU3008FQH3 (Marketplace documentation), which cannot document a runnable post-install `generate` flow until this is fixed.

## Evidence

- `src/marketplace/registrar.ts` registers recipes into the shared in-process `RecipeRegistry` via `createFileBackedRegistration(..., { sourceDirectory: packageDirectory, external: true })`, and records metadata (`kind`/`path`/`package`/`version`/`registry`) in `.toneforge-library` `registeredAssets` — it does not persist the recipe file or its package directory.
- `initializeRecipeRegistry()` discovers only built-in and external-directory recipes (`TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` / `~/.toneforge/recipes/`), not marketplace-registered assets.
- Repro: `toneforge marketplace install ui_chimes@1.0.0` succeeds, then `toneforge generate --recipe ui-chime --seed 42` in a new process reports `Unknown recipe 'ui-chime'`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After `toneforge marketplace install <pkg>@<ver>` succeeds, a new CLI process can render the installed recipes via `toneforge generate --recipe <name>` and installed stacks via `toneforge stack render` (deterministically, same seed => byte-identical output).
2. The installed recipe source/package directory is persisted (or the recipe assets are materialised into the discoverable external recipe directory) so discovery is reproducible across processes and machines.
3. Discovery is idempotent and deterministic: re-installing does not duplicate registrations, and listing/render output is byte-identical across runs.
4. An integration test spawns a real CLI child process for install and then a second child process for generate/stack render, asserting the installed assets resolve (no live network).
data.title: Marketplace installed recipes are not discoverable in a new CLI process

# Demo 11: Intelligence — Plan draft (pending producer approval)

**Prepared by:** plan (via implement epic run)
**Session:** herdr-1791458803-3290824-29548
**Effort/risk:** not yet estimated (effort-and-risk CLI returned rc=4) → the plan-approval gate requests approval.

## Seed context

- **Work item:** TF-0MLXF98WZ1LQGM5W — Demo 11: Intelligence -- Assisted Decision-Making (`issueType: epic`, `stage: idea`, `status: open`).
- **Parent:** TF-0MM4OWRQ70IWEKZ2 — Runtime Features (meta-epic).
- **Prerequisites (both complete):** Demo 7 Library (TF-0MLXF8A901W1Y176), Demo 10 Mixer (TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG).
- **Authoritative sources:** `docs/prd/INTELLIGENCE_PRD.md`, `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` §Demo 11.

## Goal

Demonstrate the reasoning layer that synthesises analysis, classification and library data to
provide actionable, explainable recommendations. Intelligence is **assistive — it suggests, the
human decides**, and it never mutates library assets.

## Existing state

- No `src/intelligence/` module exists (`grep -ril intelligence src/` returns nothing).
- CLI command groups are registered in `src/cli.yargs.ts`; each group is a module in
  `src/cli/commands/` (see `analyze.ts`, `library.ts`, `explore.ts`).
- `src/library/` provides storage/search/similarity; `src/classify/` provides labels/embeddings;
  `src/explore/` provides sweeps/recipes; `src/analyze/` provides numeric metrics.

## Acceptance Criteria (from the epic, unchanged)

1. Audit identifies coverage gaps, redundancy, and quality issues.
2. Recommendations include confidence scores and explanations.
3. Exploration suggestions reference specific recipes and seed ranges.
4. No Intelligence action modifies library data without human approval.
5. All suggestions reference actionable CLI commands.

## Proposed feature breakdown (test-first ordering)

| # | Short title | Type | Depends on | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Intelligence conformance harness | task | — | Deterministic fixtures + harness all engines are validated against; asserts determinism, JSON shape and read-only behaviour. |
| 2 | Library audit engine + `intelligence audit` | feature | 1 | End-to-end vertical slice: coverage gaps, redundancy and quality issues with an actionable suggestion. |
| 3 | Recommendation engine + `intelligence recommend` | feature | 1 | Rank library sounds for a use case with confidence scores and explanations. |
| 4 | Exploration suggestion engine + `intelligence suggest-exploration` | feature | 1 | Suggest seed ranges / surface variants for a recipe, referencing concrete CLI commands. |
| 5 | Safety, determinism & explainability hardening | task | 2, 3, 4 | Prove no command mutates library data; dry-run/logging; consistent confidence/rationale contract. |

### Feature 1 — Intelligence conformance harness (task)

- **Target outcome:** every Intelligence engine is covered by one deterministic, reusable harness.
- **Definition of done:** fixture library (≥1 category with a coverage gap, a redundancy cluster and a
  quality issue) committed under `src/test-utils/fixtures/intelligence/`; harness asserts byte-identical
  output for a fixed input+seed; asserts no library file changes; asserts the JSON contract of all three commands.
- **Minimal implementation:** fixtures; `src/intelligence/__tests__/conformance.test.ts`; shared assertion helpers.
- **Deliverables:** fixtures, harness, tests, brief README note.

### Feature 2 — Library audit engine (feature)

- **Target outcome:** `toneforge intelligence audit --library <dir>` reports gaps, redundancy and quality issues.
- **Definition of done:** detects missing combinations, similarity clusters and quality flags
  (clipping/duration/silence) using existing analyze/classify/library data; emits a structured report;
  each finding carries an actionable CLI command; human and `--json` output; unit + integration tests.
- **Minimal implementation:** `src/intelligence/audit.ts`; `src/cli/commands/intelligence.ts` (`audit`);
  register in `src/cli.yargs.ts`; docs.
- **Deliverables:** engine, CLI, tests, docs.

### Feature 3 — Recommendation engine (feature)

- **Target outcome:** `toneforge intelligence recommend --use-case "<desc>" --max-results <n>` returns ranked sounds.
- **Definition of done:** every recommendation carries a `confidence` in [0,1] and a human-readable
  explanation referencing supporting metrics; deterministic for the same library/use-case; honours
  `--max-results`; `--json` output; tests cover ranking, confidence bounds and explanations.
- **Minimal implementation:** `src/intelligence/recommend.ts` reusing library similarity/classification;
  CLI wiring; docs.
- **Deliverables:** engine, CLI, tests, docs.

### Feature 4 — Exploration suggestion engine (feature)

- **Target outcome:** `toneforge intelligence suggest-exploration --recipe <r>` suggests exploration targets.
- **Definition of done:** suggestions reference the named recipe and explicit seed ranges (e.g. current
  coverage vs. proposed range); each references an actionable `toneforge explore ...` command; `--json`
  output; tests cover seeded determinism and recipe/seed-range references.
- **Minimal implementation:** `src/intelligence/suggest-exploration.ts`; CLI wiring; docs.
- **Deliverables:** engine, CLI, tests, docs.

### Feature 5 — Safety, determinism & explainability hardening (task)

- **Target outcome:** AC4 is proven, not assumed.
- **Definition of done:** tests assert no Intelligence command writes to the library; dry-run/`--dry-run`
  supported where a write could otherwise occur; recommendations are logged and human-overrideable;
  the confidence/rationale contract is consistent across engines; docs state the read-only guarantee.
- **Minimal implementation:** read-only guards, logging, contract tests, doc updates.
- **Deliverables:** guards, tests, docs.

## Dependencies to record

- 2, 3, 4 → depend on 1
- 5 → depends on 2, 3, 4

## Open questions

None. No producer input is required for the feature breakdown itself; the only gate is approval of this
plan (effort/risk unset → approval requested).

## Approval requested

Please respond **approve** (or edit/reorder/split/merge). On approval the plan skill will create the five
children in test-first order, wire the dependency edges, run the six automated review stages plus the AC
coverage review, and estimate effort/risk. Until then this item is released to `open` with
`needsProducerReview: true`.

data.author: opencode
data.comment:
## Epic Findings Summary: Investigate and Reduce Latency of Sound Generation

### Platform & Environment
- Node.js v25.2.0
- Linux (WSL2 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, x86_64)
- vitest 4.0.18

### Methodology
All timings measured with `/usr/bin/time -f '%e'` for wall-clock, `--profile` flag for phase breakdown. Each measurement is median of 5 runs with weapon-laser-zap recipe, seed 42.

---

### Before/After Comparison

#### Dev Path (bin/dev-cli.js via tsx)

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
|--------|--------|-------|--------|
| Wall-clock | ~4.2s | ~1.5s | -64% |
| module_load phase | ~4142ms | ~1041ms | -75% |
| Render pipeline | ~28ms | ~28ms | unchanged |

#### Compiled Path (dist/cli.js)

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
|--------|--------|-------|--------|
| Wall-clock | ~0.96s | ~0.44s | -54% |
| module_load phase | ~940ms | ~340ms (est.) | -64% |
| Render pipeline | ~28ms | ~28ms | unchanged |

---

### Optimizations Implemented

#### F1: Pipeline Profiling Infrastructure (TF-0MM0YTYLE0BN0YR9) [completed]
- Added `--profile` flag with 10-phase timing breakdown
- Zero-cost singleton profiler when disabled
- 9 unit tests

#### F2: End-to-End Benchmark Suite (TF-0MM0YUBFR0MCXGLE) [completed]
- Shell script (scripts/benchmark-cli.sh) with mean/median/min/max/p95
- 3 vitest bench files (renderer, WAV encoder, recipe registry)
- Established baselines showing module_load is 99.3% of dev path latency

#### F3: Lazy Recipe Loading (TF-0MM0YURXB03NLOE3) [completed]
- Converted all 18 recipes from eager imports to lazy factoryLoader thunks
- Added LazyRecipeRegistration interface with discriminated union RegistryEntry
- Only the requested recipe is imported at runtime
- Eliminated ~780ms of Tone.js import per unused recipe

#### F4: Direct-to-Device Playback (TF-0MM0YVAEL00NKHNT) [completed]
- Added stdin piping for paplay, aplay, ffplay (bypasses temp file I/O)
- Automatic fallback to temp-file path when piping unavailable
- 13 unit tests

#### F5: Compiled CLI Build Optimization (TF-0MM0YVPHS0H3MMJH) [completed]
- Lazy-loaded marked-terminal/chalk/marked in output.ts (was ~590ms eager import)
- renderMarkdown() and outputMarkdown() made async
- esbuild bundling evaluated but found NOT beneficial (bottleneck is npm dep import cost, not file resolution)
- Compiled path median: 0.96s -> 0.44s (54% reduction)

#### F6: Parallel Stack Layer Rendering (TF-0MM0YW1IS0V95DIV) [closed - not needed]
- Profiled 3-layer explosion_heavy stack: 107ms total sequential render
- Theoretical parallel savings: ~58ms (~13% of total compiled-path time)
- Not justified given complexity/determinism risk vs small absolute savings

---

### Latency Breakdown (Final State, Compiled Path)

| Phase | Time (ms) | % of Total |
|-------|-----------|------------|
| Module load | ~340 | 77% |
| Recipe resolution + factory import | ~5 | 1% |
| Context creation + graph build | ~21 | 5% |
| Render | ~14 | 3% |
| WAV encode | ~18 | 4% |
| File write | ~16 | 4% |
| Other overhead | ~26 | 6% |
| **Total** | **~440** | **100%** |

---

### Remaining Bottlenecks

1. **node-web-audio-api import (~100ms)** - Imported by core/renderer.js. Cannot be easily deferred since it is needed for every generate command.
2. **Node.js startup (~60ms)** - Fixed overhead, cannot be optimized.
3. **npm dependency loading (~180ms)** - Remaining npm deps (commander-like parsing, fs, path, etc.) that cannot be lazy-loaded.
4. **tsx overhead (~600-700ms additional on dev path)** - Inherent to on-the-fly TypeScript compilation. Mitigated by using compiled path in production.

### Trade-off Analysis

The single most impactful optimization was lazy recipe loading (F3), which eliminated the need to import Tone.js (~780ms) for every unused recipe. The second most impactful was lazy-loading marked-terminal (F5), eliminating ~590ms of import overhead for commands that do not render markdown (which is most commands).

esbuild bundling was thoroughly evaluated but rejected — the bottleneck is in the V8 evaluation cost of npm dependencies, not in file resolution. A single bundle or code-split bundle produced identical startup times to the plain tsc output.

### Future Optimization Opportunities

No new work items created — remaining bottlenecks are either fixed overhead (Node.js startup, core dependency imports) or require architectural changes outside the scope of this investigation (e.g., a persistent daemon process, native addon for audio rendering, or the planned real-time engine TF-0MLYX9DP51U7AQDK).

## F5 Build Optimization Results

### Approach
Lazy-loaded heavy dependencies in output.ts (marked, marked-terminal, chalk) which were adding ~590ms of module-load overhead at CLI startup. The marked-terminal import chain (cli-highlight 410ms + node-emoji 72ms + others) was the dominant compiled-path bottleneck after lazy recipe loading (F3).

esbuild bundling (single-file and code-split) was tested but did NOT reduce module_load time — the bottleneck is npm dependency import cost, not file-count resolution. Lazy loading was the correct approach.

### Changes
- output.ts: Converted top-level imports of chalk, marked, marked-terminal to lazy dynamic imports inside renderMarkdown()
- output.ts: renderMarkdown() and outputMarkdown() are now async (return Promise)
- output.ts: Added getTerminalRendererOptions() with cached lazy init
- cli.ts: Made all 14 printXxxHelp() functions async, added await to all 32 call sites and outputMarkdown() calls
- output.test.ts: Updated all 15 tests (setTtyOverride, renderMarkdown, outputMarkdown) with async/await

- Median: ~0.96s

**After (lazy loading marked-terminal + chalk):**
- Runs: 0.41s, 0.45s, 0.62s, 0.44s, 0.37s

data.author: opencode
data.comment:
## F6 Parallel Stack Rendering - Not Needed (Documented)

### Profiling Results

Profiled the explosion_heavy preset (3 layers: impact-crack, rumble-body, debris-tail) with seed 42 on the compiled path:

**Stack render (sequential, 3 layers):** 107ms total

**Individual layer render times:**
- impact-crack: graph_build->render 6.2ms, render phase 15.2ms
- rumble-body: graph_build->render 19.0ms, render phase 47.7ms  
- debris-tail: graph_build->render 2.8ms, render phase 43.4ms
- Sum of render phases: ~106ms (matches the 107ms stack render time)

**Theoretical parallel improvement:**
With Promise.all, the render phase would be bounded by the slowest layer (~48ms) instead of the sum (~106ms), saving ~58ms. However:

1. The absolute time saved (~58ms) is small compared to module_load (~440ms compiled, ~1900ms dev)
2. The 3-layer stack is the largest preset in the project
3. Web Audio API OfflineAudioContext may not safely support parallel instances in node-web-audio-api (risk of shared state issues)
4. Determinism testing would become more complex

### Conclusion

Stack rendering is NOT a significant bottleneck. The render phase for a 3-layer stack is ~107ms out of a total compiled-path execution time of ~440ms (24%). Parallelizing would save ~58ms (13% of total), with added complexity and determinism risk. The optimization is not justified.

Closing as 'not needed - documented' per acceptance criteria.

Planning complete. 4 child features created with linear dependency chain:

1. **EmbeddingProvider Interface & AnalysisMetricsProvider** (TF-0MM60CEOU0CKO0N9) — Define interface, implement default 7-dim metrics provider.
2. **Classification Engine Embedding Integration** (TF-0MM60CLU60VKXCPS) — Extend ClassificationResult with embedding field, integrate provider into engine, update CLI paths.
3. **Embedding-Based Library Similarity** (TF-0MM60CRRV0R70M8F) — Replace ad-hoc 4-metric hybrid distance with embedding-based Euclidean distance.
4. **Library Regeneration & End-to-End Validation** (TF-0MM60D2J91UKPKHT) — Delete and regenerate library, spot-check similarity results, run full test suite.

Scope reductions from original description (per user direction):
- No auto-backfill (library will be regenerated from scratch).
- No --method flag / no 3-mode switching (embeddings are the only similarity method).
- Sync interface (async deferred to future ML provider work).
- Fixed 7-dim vectors with 0 for missing metrics.

Open questions: None.

data.comment:
Implemented Library Core module. Commit d706376 on branch feature/TF-0MM1GNRXW04CP2FI-library-core.

Files created:
- src/library/types.ts: LibraryEntry, LibraryIndex, LibraryPreset, LibraryProvenance, LibraryFiles, LibraryFilter types
- src/library/index-store.ts: loadIndex, saveIndex, addToIndex, getFromIndex, removeFromIndex, listFromIndex, clearIndexCache
- src/library/storage.ts: addEntry, getEntry, listEntries, removeEntry, countEntries, buildEntry, entryId, readEntryMetadata, entryWavExists
- src/library/index.ts: Public API re-exports
- src/library/__tests__/index-store.test.ts: 22 tests
- src/library/__tests__/storage.test.ts: 24 tests

All acceptance criteria satisfied:
- LibraryEntry type defined with all required fields (id, recipe, seed, category, duration, tags, analysis, classification, preset, provenance, files, promotedAt)
- addEntry() writes WAV + metadata JSON to .toneforge-library/<category>/, updates index, returns entry
- getEntry(id) retrieves by ID from in-memory index
- listEntries(filter?) returns entries with optional category/recipe/tags filtering
- Idempotent add (same candidate ID returns existing entry)
- Category derived from classification or defaults to uncategorized
- Index loaded into memory on first access, written back on mutation
- Pattern follows src/explore/persistence.ts conventions

Full test suite: 1135 tests passing, 0 type errors.

3. Existing automation intact — existing automation tests still green
4. Validation no longer rejects sequences — schema tests
5. Unit/integration tests — tonegraph-schema.test.ts, tonegraph.test.ts, tonegraph.integration.test.ts
Full suite green (2572 tests, 129 files) at the pushed commit.

Stabilized the browser smoke e2e. Commit 8079f00 pushed to dev.

## Investigation
- File-backed recipes are already discoverable in the web build via `web/src/browser-recipe-registry.ts` (`import.meta.glob` over `presets/recipes/*.yaml`, added by TF-0MUVK0MGO001P2OF) and covered by `web/test/browser-recipe-registry.test.ts`.
- `web/e2e/tonegraph-smoke.spec.ts` is deterministic (selects the `mvp-1` demo, act 1) and asserts a non-zero rendered buffer with no `Unknown recipe` or Node-only console errors.
- Local results: root suite 2736 passed; web unit suite 546 passed; full web e2e 20 passed.

## Fix: busy default port no longer aborts the run
The default e2e port (3000) is frequently occupied (e.g. another project's dev server), which made Playwright abort with "port is already used" before any test ran.
- Added `web/scripts/select-port.ts` — `isPortFree`/`findFreePort` (async `net` probe) plus `findFreePortSync` (child-process probe, for the synchronously-evaluated config).
- `web/playwright.config.ts` now selects the first free port at or after 3000 unless `PORT` is set, and passes it to the web server via `env`. The chosen port is cached in `TF_E2E_PORT` so Playwright's worker processes (which re-evaluate the config) use the same port as the main process.
- Added `web/test/select-port.test.ts` (4 tests) and documented the behaviour plus the smoke coverage in `docs/browser-usage.md`.

## Verification
- `npm run build` (tsc) clean; web e2e helper typechecks.
- Root suite: 2736 passed. Web unit suite: 546 passed (+4 new).
- Full web e2e run with port 3000 occupied and `PORT` unset: 20 passed (auto-selected a free port). Explicit `PORT=3123` also passes.

Added a CI job for the web Playwright e2e suite. Commit 3589cbe pushed to dev.

## What changed
- Added `.github/workflows/web-playwright.yml` (new — dev had no CI workflows): runs on push to `dev`/`main` and on PRs touching `web/`, `presets/`, `src/`, or the lockfiles; `workflow_dispatch` for manual runs; concurrency cancels superseded runs. Steps: checkout, Node 22 (npm cache), `npm ci` (root + web), `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox`, `npm run build` (web), `CI=true npx playwright test`, then uploads `web/playwright-report` and `web/test-results` artifacts (always).
- Updated `web/playwright.config.ts`: CI retries = 2 (local 0) and, on CI, an HTML reporter alongside the list reporter, so failures are retried and reports/traces are produced for upload.
- Documented the workflow in `docs/browser-usage.md`.

## Environment / preset assets
Playwright starts the web server itself (`node dist-server/index.js`). File-backed recipes are inlined into the client bundle at build time by the Vite `yamlRecipePlugin` + `import.meta.glob` in `web/src/browser-recipe-registry.ts`, so no separate static-asset copy step is needed.

## Verification
- Workflow YAML parses and lists the expected triggers/jobs/steps.
- Ran the exact CI command sequence locally with `CI=true`: `npm run test:e2e:ci --prefix web` → 20 passed (port 3000 occupied; the auto-port change selected a free port). `web/playwright-report/index.html` was generated.
- Root suite 2736 passed; web unit suite 546 passed; `npm run build` clean.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Root cause confirmed: `implement.py` `phase_start` symlinks the main checkout's real node_modules into each worktree (`<worktree>/node_modules -> <main>/node_modules`). The `.gitignore` rule `node_modules/` (trailing slash) matches only a *directory*, not a *symlink* — so the worktree's `git add -A` in `git_commit` staged the symlink and pushed it to `dev` via commit f40ea87. When the worktree is later removed, the main checkout's `node_modules` is left as a self-referential link, breaking all builds/tests.

Fix implemented:
- `.gitignore`: added `node_modules` (no trailing slash) so the worktree symlink is ignored; also `.implement_state.json`.
- `git rm --cached node_modules .implement_state.json` to untrack both from the index.
- `test/repo-hygiene.test.ts`: regression guard asserting no node_modules path is tracked, the symlink is ignored by check-ignore, the implement state file is untracked, and node_modules is never a self-referential link.

data.comment:
## Implementation notes — e2e failure diagnostics

### What changed
- **New** `web/e2e/helpers/diagnostics.ts` — shared capture/format/wait helpers:
  - `captureConsole(page)` records console messages + uncaught page errors (incl. `Unknown recipe` warnings).
  - pure helpers `stripAnsi`, `isShellErrorLine`, `extractShellErrors`, `findUnknownRecipeWarnings`, `selectDiagnosticConsole`, `formatTimeoutDiagnostics` (unit-tested).
  - `getTerminalText` merges the xterm accessibility tree and DOM rows (the a11y tree alone can drop earlier rows when a long prompt wraps).
  - `waitForTerminalText` fails fast, naming a detected shell error; `waitForRenderedBufferLength` fails fast, naming the `Unknown recipe` warning.
- **New** `web/test/diagnostics.test.ts` — 15 unit tests of the pure helpers.
- **Extend** `web/e2e/tonegraph-smoke.spec.ts` — uses `captureConsole`; asserts no `Unknown recipe` warning after Run (the observable proof the registry resolved `ui-scifi-confirm`); render timeouts now name that warning.
- **Extend** `web/e2e/tutorial.spec.ts` — shared terminal waits; new test `PTY environment exposes a resolvable toneforge command`; banner test (AC5) retained; removed the fixed 2s/1s sleeps in the full walkthrough (explicit Run-button `toBeEnabled` wait instead).
- **`web/playwright.config.ts`** — `trace` now `{ mode: "retain-on-failure", snapshots: false }`. The DOM-snapshot capture races xterm.js's DOM renderer and can drop the `ToneForge Terminal` banner under long paths, which made the banner assertion fail intermittently; screenshots/sources/console/network traces are retained.

- Directory resolution for `list sequences` / `list stacks` with precedence `--dir <path>` → `TONEFORGE_SEQUENCES_DIR` / `TONEFORGE_STACKS_DIR` → repo default, mirroring the existing `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` pattern in `src/core/recipe.ts`.

- Golden/stack fixture harnesses are refactored onto the shared helper so they inherit the artefact exclusion.
- New option/environment variables documented.

- Parent AC 1 → C2; AC 2 → C2; AC 3 → C2/C3; AC 4 → C2/C3; AC 5 → C2.

## Plan

Deliver an audible, render-backed runtime demo (PRD §19) with headless verification.

1. **Scenario preset** — `presets/runtime/footsteps.json` (versioned): state machine (idle/walk/run/sprint), context dimensions (surface), short walk/run/sprint sequences using a generic `footstep` event, a declarative recipe-resolver template (`footstep` + surface → `footstep-{surface}`), and scripted steps (walk on stone → walk on gravel → sprint on gravel).
2. **Scenario loader** — `src/runtime/scenario.ts`: types, validation, `parseRuntimeScenario`/`loadRuntimeScenario`, template resolver.
3. **Render-backed bridge** — `src/runtime/audio.ts`: drive the runtime through the scripted steps with a deterministic clock, collect `event_fire` events, build a `SimulationResult`, mix via the existing `renderSequence`, plus a browser `AudioBufferSourceNode` scheduling helper. No second synthesis engine.
4. **CLI** — `toneforge runtime demo [--scenario <path>] [--seed <n>] [--output <dir>] [--json]`: play in Node via `playAudio`; `--output` exports `runtime-demo.wav` + `timeline.json`; `--json` prints the timeline. Wired through `src/cli.runtime.ts` + `src/cli.yargs.ts` + `src/cli/commands/runtime.ts`.
5. **Tests** — scenario parsing; determinism (same seed → same log + samples); state/context buffers differ; event log records recipe changes (footstep-stone → footstep-gravel, walk → sprint); browser scheduling helper; CLI integration (help/validation/JSON/WAV export/playback mock).
6. **Docs** — RUNTIME_PRD §19 delivered note, README, CLI help, browser-usage, CLI cutover checklist, `demos/runtime.md` + index.
7. Build → tests → commit → push dev.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
implement — design notes (pre-commit).

**AC1 (audible modulation).** SFX parameter values are applied as deterministic DSP on the freshly-rendered buffer each transport iteration (pitch resample → one-pole low-pass → gain × intensity), so a change is audible on the next loop pass (iteration-granular, per the scope note). Chosen over render-key overrides because `renderPreset` overrides only honour recipe-declared parameter names, and no recipe declares intensity/gain/pitch/filter.

**Voice identity.** The runtime does not yet track active voices, so the sound `id` is defined to be the event's **resolved recipe name** (e.g. `footstep-gravel`). `runtime.setSfxParameter(id, ...)` values for that id are applied to every render of that recipe. Documented in RUNTIME_PRD §19.9.

**Command surface.** Added `param <id> <name> <value>` to the live session; help updated.

**AC2 (service mode).** New `src/runtime/service.ts` controller (injectable signal source) + `runtime start --serve`: no TTY required, stays alive after stdin EOF, clean shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM or `quit`. A referenced keep-alive interval holds the Node event loop open (a pending await alone exits with code 13).

**AC3.** Determinism tests added; docs updated (RUNTIME_PRD §19.9/§19.10, README, browser-usage).

The project's web Vitest config already uses an explicit `testTimeout`, so this is consistent.

**Discovered same-class flake (fixed inline to meet AC3):** `src/demo/machine-use.integration.test.ts` ('empty candidate list exits 0...') has an explicit 15s test timeout and spawns multiple CLI/`npx` invocations; it reproducibly timed out under sustained host contention (load avg ~31 on 16 CPUs, largely from other projects'/worktrees' test runs). Raised its explicit timeout 15s -> 30s to match its 30s execFile budget. This is a minimal, same-class timeout alignment; the test's assertions are unchanged.

- Target test in isolation: PASS (3346ms) — AC2.
- Three consecutive full-suite runs under sustained external host contention (load avg ~31–33): 158 files / 3880 tests passed each time, target test included, no timeout — AC1/AC3.
- `npm run build` (tsc): clean.

No documentation change required: the fix is confined to Vitest configuration (`vitest.config.ts`) and one test file's explicit timeout. No user-facing or developer docs describe this test's timeout/parallelism behaviour, so there is nothing to update to match. Recorded per AC4.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Design decisions and assumptions for the validate/compile CLI:

1. Added new command modules src/cli/commands/validate.ts and src/cli/commands/compile.ts, wired through src/cli.yargs.ts (registration + FRAMEWORK_COMMANDS) and src/cli.runtime.ts (dispatch + help).
2. validate defaults: --library .toneforge-library, --ruleset web, --strictness warning. Exit code 1 only when the report is build-blocking (error-level finding), so it can gate CI; exit 0 otherwise.
3. compile requires at least one of --target or --rules. --rules accepts a built-in name (web_defaults, mobile_aggressive) OR a path to a JSON ruleset file. --target overrides the ruleset target. --output is required unless --dry-run; dry-run defaults output to dist/<target> but writes nothing.
4. CLI errors are emitted as {"error": "..."} on stderr when --json is set, and human-readable text otherwise.
5. Added example ruleset files presets/compile/web_defaults.json and presets/compile/mobile_aggressive.json (mirroring the built-ins) so the epic-level example invocations work; a test asserts they match the built-ins.
6. Updated docs/validator.md and docs/compiler.md with CLI sections, and synced docs/cli-cutover-checklist.md with FRAMEWORK_COMMANDS (also added the previously-missing intelligence/intent/memory rows so scripts/check-cli-coverage.ts passes).
7. Tests: src/cli.validate.integration.test.ts, src/cli.compile.integration.test.ts, plus two yargs child-process routing tests. Full suite green.

Pipeline: fetch -> integrity (path-safety + existence + SHA-256 + optional declared-hash compare) -> validation gate -> dependency resolution (F4, opt-in) -> register (content-addressed assets, provenance, exact version lock). Design decisions / assumptions:
